question: Should OpenClaw adopt generic ordered configuration authority in core, and which loading, mutation, and upgrade guarantees must be fixed in the accepted contract?
rationale: The proposal creates a permanent cross-cutting configuration ownership model whose scope and compatibility behavior cannot be selected safely by automated review.

options.title: Refine In Draft
options.body: Keep this PR open and make source loading, write enforcement, fallback, reload, and upgrade behavior decision-ready before acceptance.

options.title: Accept With Follow-Up
options.body: Approve the authority model while explicitly assigning bounded unresolved mechanics to a linked implementation issue.

options.title: Decline Core Ownership
options.body: Continue handling deployment-owned configuration through host-specific systems outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Refine In Draft
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open and make source loading, write enforcement, fallback, reload, and upgrade behavior decision-ready before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and formalized this repository's RFC acceptance process, making them the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the acceptance decision.
